chapter: The Los Angeles music scene in the early 1930s
title: Lionel Hampton as a powerful young drummer
summary: He remembers recording with the Spikes group, when Hampton's drums were too loud and had to be put out in the bowls, and when Hampton took up vibes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Lionel Hampton was on the scene then and I know you recorded with him when you recorded with the Spikes Brothers.
That's right.
Tell us a little bit about Lionel. He's still going and just tremendous....
I had little difficulty in consoling him on the record, he was naturally loud, they didn't have a place to put him, and one of the directors said, put him out in the bowls.
Was that because he was so strong on the drums?
That's right.
He was not playing the vibes at this time?
No.
The drums overpowered the rest of the band.
That's right. The director made a remark, he said put him out in the bowls.
He was so powerful they thought well, he can't stay in here and record.
That's right.
Tell us some more about Lionel, who is indeed a legend.
He was powerful on the drums; he was what we called a noisy drummer.
Did he swing?
Yeah, he could swing.
Did Lionel ever have his own orchestra at this time? Did he have an orchestra in the early thirties?
No.
He was just digging around with the rest of the guys; is that right?
That's right.
You could recognize his unusual talent at this time?
Oh, yes.
About when do you recall him playing the vibes?
He started out around this time with the vibes.
